land.text: the Gaza Strip, which after Israel's withdrawal of 2005 'was left under the control of the Palestinian Authority'

predecessors.note: Hamas won the legislative elections of 25 January 2006 and took the Strip from Fatah-controlled forces on 11-15 June 2007.

capitals.name: Gaza City
capitals.note: The Gaza Strip page calls Gaza City the capital and largest city; the Governance page names no official seat for the Hamas government.

correction.text: the whole Gaza Strip, over which Hamas took full control on 15 June 2007

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe: Cliopatria's Gaza/Hamas row begins in 2014, seven years after Hamas took the Strip (11-15 June 2007; the Gaza Strip page says 'By 14 June 2007' Hamas 'fully controlled' it). Hamas rejected the dismissal of its government and kept governing Gaza separately, the Palestinian Authority being limited to the West Bank. Infobox area 365 km2.

correction.text: the whole Gaza Strip as one outline

keyframe_review.note: 154.8 km2 against the infobox 365 km2 (ratio 0.42, beyond a factor of two): the shape is a single patch (34.30-34.47 E, 31.34-31.46 N) that covers less than half of a Strip which runs 41 km along the coast and 6-12 km inland, so it is too small, not merely coarse. Correct it to the whole Strip (three cells on the r5 grid, 759 km2 as the gazetteer counts them). The page records no change of extent in 2014 (the 2014 unity government of 2 June 2014 and the 8 July 2014 war do not move the line).

correction.text: the whole Gaza Strip as one outline, with the Israeli-held zones of the war drawn by the contest event

keyframe_review.note: Same 154.8 km2 patch as 2014-2023 against 365 km2, the same correction. In 2024 Israel's ground invasion (begun in early November 2023) had weakened Hamas control, the Israeli government said on 6 January 2024 that Hamas rule in northern Gaza was eliminated, and Hamas began reviving some governing functions in parts of Gaza City from late January 2024; the page gives no map of the Israeli-held zones (Netzarim, Philadelphi, Rafah are not on it).

region.text: the Gaza Strip, 365 km2, 41 km long and 6-12 km wide

ledger.note: 2007: Hamas takes the Gaza Strip. Hamas began taking control of the territory from Fatah-controlled forces on 11 June 2007; on 14 June Abbas dissolved the unity government, declared a state of emergency and dismissed Haniyeh; on 15 June 2007 Hamas took full control of the Strip. Hamas kept governing separately and the Palestinian Authority's reach shrank to the West Bank. (The Gaza Strip page says Hamas 'fully controlled' the Strip by 14 June.)

region.text: the Gaza Strip, 365 km2, 41 km long and 6-12 km wide

ledger.note: 2023: Israel's ground invasion of the Gaza Strip begins. The Governance page has Israel's ground invasion beginning in early November 2023 and weakening Hamas's control; the Gaza Strip page has Hamas attacking Israel on 7 October 2023 and Israel declaring war on 9 October, and says Israel has occupied large parts of the Strip since October 2023. The page names no zone except northern Gaza (6 January 2024), so the contest zone is the whole Strip as my reading. Unpaired in 2024: no ceasefire is recorded before the 19 January 2025 truce.

wars.name: Battle of Gaza (2007)

zones.text: the Gaza Strip, 365 km2, 41 km long and 6-12 km wide

wars.outcome: Hamas took full control of the Gaza Strip between 11 and 15 June 2007; Abbas dismissed the Haniyeh government on 14 June and appointed Salam Fayyad; the Palestinian Authority was left with the West Bank.
wars.note: Mecca agreement of 8 February 2007 and the March 2007 unity government preceded it.

wars.name: Gaza War (2008-2009)
wars.outcome: The Gaza Strip page gives only the Israeli ground invasion of 3 January 2009; it states no result and no territorial change.
wars.note: Included so the reviewer sees it was considered; the Governance page records an Israeli curtailing of travel, goods and fuel in January 2008.

wars.name: 2014 Gaza War
wars.outcome: Israel launched Operation Protective Edge on 8 July 2014, a seven-week conflict; the page gives no end date, no ground held and no territorial change.
wars.note: The Hamas-Fatah unity government (the Third Hamdallah Government, 2 June 2014 to 17 October 2016) failed to organize elections or reunify the territories (Governance page).

wars.name: Gaza war (2023-present)

zones.text: the Gaza Strip, 365 km2, 41 km long and 6-12 km wide

wars.outcome: Ongoing at 2024: Israel's ground invasion began in early November 2023; on 6 January 2024 the Israeli government said Hamas rule in northern Gaza had been eliminated; Hamas began reviving some governing functions in parts of Gaza City from late January 2024.
wars.note: After the map's last year: a ceasefire from 19 January to 18 March 2025, Hamas losing most of the Strip in June 2025 (Operation Gideon's Chariots), the IDF holding about 53% after the October 2025 plan (64% in an April 2026 infobox).

certainty.note: The Strip is a fixed enclave (about 51 km of border with Israel, 11 km with Egypt along the Philadelphi corridor) but the pages name no treaty or survey line, so this is the outline, not a dated record. Exceptions: from November 2023 the Israeli-held zones are a contest, not a border; the pages do not map them.

sources.title: Governance of the Gaza Strip
sources.note: June 2007 takeover (11-15 June), the PA split, the 2014 unity government, the 2023-2024 invasion. Silent on the area, the 2005 disengagement dates, the Netzarim and Philadelphi corridors and the seat of the Hamas government.

notes: Pages used: 2 (the budget is 1-2). 'Gaza/Hamas' is a Cliopatria aggregate of a territory and the movement that has governed it; treated here as the de facto Hamas administration of the Gaza Strip, type rebel (hatched in its own colour as a regime holding land against the recognised Palestinian Authority), starting in June 2007 and not in 2014 as the row does. Not settled: (1) the Cliopatria shape is 154.8 km2, 42% of the 365 km2 infobox area; all three keyframes correct it to the whole Strip; (2) the Palestinian Authority has no dossier ('palestinians' in polities.csv is a single 1948 shape); a dossier 'palestinian-national-authority' (1994-) is needed as the counterpart of the 2007 founding, and Israel's occupation of the Strip until the 2005 withdrawal ('In 2005, Israel withdrew from the Gaza Strip', no day given on either page) belongs to state-of-israel's dossier; (3) the Governance page says Hamas took full control on 15 June 2007 and the Gaza Strip page by 14 June 2007: the dossier uses the Governance page's 15 June; (4) the zones Israel held in 2023-2024 (Netzarim Corridor, Philadelphi Corridor, Rafah in May 2024) are not on the pages opened, so only a whole-Strip contest is recorded and it is unpaired; (5) the Hamas seat is not named on the Governance page, Gaza City is called the capital on the Strip page, used for the capital dot; (6) rulers omitted: the pages give Haniyeh (June 2007 to February 2017 as Hamas leader in Gaza, head of government 2007-2014) and Yahya Sinwar (until October 2024) without start dates for the latter. Gazetteer: {admin1 Gaza Strip} resolves (it is also the Natural Earth name). Counterparts needing dossiers: palestinian-national-authority.
